doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

chapter: Views on drummers and the state of jazz
title: Drum machines and synthetic instruments
summary: He thinks the time of electronic drums has passed and studios still want real drummers.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: What’s your feeling when you listen to let’s say light jazz, contemporary jazz, that obviously have a little box providing all the drums?

As far as what I call synthetic instruments, I think the height is passed. I really do. I think in studios, I get calls to do jingles because they want the human factor. They don’t want the sterile time or the sound, they want the real person. And I think like electronic drums, I think the time for that is passed. We tried it, it came out, and while it was a nice toy, but
a keyboard player in a lounge that has drums programmed into it, I think is almost circus- like now to the public. They want to hear, they want to see the real players.
